contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_director_insights, get_coaching_digest, run_smart_search, get_team_synthesis
contexts.description: An AI coaching layer that monitors agent behavior patterns and surfaces momentum insights, behavioral drift warnings, and actionable suggestions for improving persona performance. The director synthesizes data from multiple sources (executions, certifications, incidents) to produce a periodic coaching digest visible in the overview sidebar.
contexts.name: ai-director

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: run_health_check, stream_healing_session, get_healing_status
contexts.description: Detects and auto-repairs execution failures by streaming an LLM-generated diagnosis and corrective patch. The healing engine inspects error traces, proposes a fix, and optionally re-runs the failed execution with the patch applied. The UI surfaces healing status in the execution detail view and the persona health monitoring panel.
contexts.name: ai-healing

contexts.api_surface: Tauri window commands; system state commands
contexts.description: The outermost application scaffold — Tauri window setup, React root mount, sidebar navigation, layout containers, and the global command palette. It determines which feature surface is rendered based on the active sidebar section and manages the top-level UI state (theme, density, sidebar collapsed state). The `preloadPersistedLocaleBeforeMount` call here prevents non-English first-paint flicker.
contexts.name: app-shell

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: process_media, transcribe_audio, save_artifact, get_artist_sessions
contexts.description: Audio and video generation plugin — wraps FFmpeg for media processing, provides speech transcription, and manages audio persistence. Used by personas that produce audio artifacts or need to transcribe recorded inputs. The schema policy enforces output constraints for generated media.
contexts.name: artist-plugin

contexts.api_surface: npm scripts; GitHub Actions CI; lefthook hooks
contexts.description: All build, CI, and developer-tooling scripts — Vite config, Tauri build configs (lite/stable), lefthook git hooks, codegen pipeline runner, asset optimization, i18n coverage gate, and the check-doc-sync hook. This context glues together the multi-step build pipeline from TypeScript check through Rust compilation to installer packaging.
contexts.name: build-tooling

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: run_certification, get_certification_results, get_certification_verdict
contexts.description: Quality gate system that runs structured certification checks against personas to produce verdicts (LIVE / DEGRADED / STALLED). Certification runs evaluate execution quality, SLA compliance, and behavioral consistency, producing a score and a detailed breakdown. Results feed into the fleet health overview and block deployments when thresholds are not met.
contexts.name: certification-system

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: send_chat_message, stream_chat_response, get_chat_history, add_annotation
contexts.description: Real-time conversational chat interface for interacting with a persona — sending messages, receiving streamed LLM replies, and viewing the conversation thread with annotations. Manages a per-persona chat history and supports background chat sessions that run independently of the foreground view. The chat slice keeps message state; the chatSlice handles background queues.
contexts.name: chat-interface

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: companion_chat, get_companion_proactive_nudges, submit_decision, transcribe_voice, get_companion_observability
contexts.description: The Athena companion AI — a proactive assistant embedded in the app that monitors fleet state, surfaces nudges, answers questions in natural language, and assists with complex decisions. It runs its own execution loop with voice input/output, sensory inputs, and plugin integrations, and coordinates with the main engine via the fleet bridge. TTS is provided by three local engine backends: Kokoro, Pocket, and Sherpa-ONNX, each with their own installer and model catalog.
contexts.name: companion-ai

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_connectors, create_connector, update_connector, test_connector, get_channel_delivery
contexts.description: Manages integrations with external services (Slack, GitHub, email, etc.) as connectors that personas use to send and receive messages. The connectors UI shows connection status, lets users configure delivery rules, and exposes automation flows per connector. The channel delivery subsystem routes execution outputs to the right connector endpoints.
contexts.name: connector-management

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: forage_credentials, negotiate_credential, propose_schema, run_nl_query, get_credential_design
contexts.description: Design-time intelligence that helps users wire the right credentials to a persona during the build wizard — suggesting credential types, validating that required scopes are present, and negotiating the best available credential when multiple options exist. The foraging system discovers candidate credentials from the vault; the negotiator ranks them by fit.
contexts.name: credential-design

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_credentials, create_credential, update_credential, delete_credential, test_credential
contexts.description: Local-first encrypted credential store that saves API keys, tokens, and secrets with AES-256-GCM encryption — credentials never leave the machine. The vault UI provides a catalog browser, credential creation wizard, and connection status indicators. The Rust side enforces encryption at rest via the SQLite vault schema and provides the IPC surface for reading credentials into the engine at execution time.
contexts.name: credential-vault

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_kpis, create_kpi, measure_kpi, derive_kpi, run_autopilot, scan_codebase_context
contexts.description: Developer-facing tools for running the agent fleet autonomously — KPI outcome tracking (dev_kpis, measurements, goal linkage), autopilot configuration, prompt lab experimentation, and the dev-tools scanner that discovers codebase context for personas working on code. The KPI layer sits above goals and drives the evaluation-and-derivation pipeline.
contexts.name: dev-tools-kpis

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_events, subscribe_events, get_sla_status, get_event_digest
contexts.description: Real-time event log viewer that shows all system events (execution lifecycle, connector triggers, SLA breaches, messages) in a filterable, searchable stream. Backed by the Tauri event bus and supplemented by the SLA tracking subsystem that measures promise-vs-delivery time windows. Events are written by the engine and read here for operator visibility.
contexts.name: event-monitoring

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_executions, get_execution_detail, get_execution_steps, get_execution_messages
contexts.description: Frontend UI for browsing, searching, and inspecting past persona execution records. The list view shows paginated execution runs with status badges, cost, and duration; the detail inspector shows per-step breakdowns, token counts, and raw LLM messages. Data is fetched via the executions API and cached in the execution Zustand slice.
contexts.name: execution-history

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: run_persona, cancel_execution, get_execution_status, stream_execution_events
contexts.description: The Rust-side core engine that spawns, schedules, and drives persona executions — invoking LLM inference, dispatching tool calls, and writing execution events to SQLite. It manages the full lifecycle from queue admission through result persistence, including budget enforcement, retry logic, and the event bus that feeds real-time updates to the frontend. All other execution-facing features depend on this module.
contexts.name: execution-runner

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_execution_trace, get_replay_snapshot
contexts.description: Visual timeline replay and trace inspector that lets users scrub through an execution step by step, seeing LLM turns, tool invocations, and branching decisions. The replay sandbox computes diffs between steps using a web worker, and the trace view renders an interactive graph. Designed for debugging and post-mortem analysis of persona behavior.
contexts.name: execution-trace

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_fleet_status, get_fleet_liveness, send_channel_message_from_monitor
contexts.description: Real-time fleet monitoring surface that shows all running personas and teams with live status columns — current execution state, last heartbeat, liveness verdict, and goal progress. The monitor includes always-on channel message entry for operator interventions and pop-up notifications for incoming channel events. Drives the FleetLivenessWatchdog that detects stalled teams.
contexts.name: fleet-monitor

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_persona_glyph, update_persona_glyph, get_capability_catalog
contexts.description: Visual composer for persona glyphs — the graphical representation of a persona's capabilities assembled from component blocks. Users drag capability components (tools, connectors, behaviors) into a command panel to build the persona's functional identity. The glyph is stored as a structured JSON config and is the canonical visual summary of a persona.
contexts.name: glyph-composer

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_fleet_pulse, get_recent_executions, get_roadmap_status
contexts.description: The home screen shown on launch — a cockpit of 40+ configurable widgets (quick-run tiles, fleet pulse, recent executions, power-move spotlights, roadmap pills) plus the first-run welcome screen with setup cards. The welcome flow guides new users through connecting their first credential and adopting a starter persona.
contexts.name: home-welcome

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_review_requests, submit_review_decision, get_review_history
contexts.description: Pause-and-review gates in the execution pipeline where personas request human approval before proceeding. Reviewers see the pending decision context, can accept or reject with an optional directive, and Athena learns from each resolution. Accepted reviews resume the blocked execution; rejections trigger a retry or escalation path.
contexts.name: human-review

contexts.api_surface: Internal hook: useTranslation(); CI script: check-coverage.mjs
contexts.description: 14-language internationalization pipeline: the English source locale (11,500+ keys), per-section lazy chunk splitting, a TypeScript type tree generated from `en.json`, and the `useTranslation` proxy hook. Non-English locales fall back to English per key, translation teams catch up asynchronously. The check-coverage CI gate rejects stale keys.
contexts.name: i18n-system

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_incidents, create_incident, resolve_incident, escalate_incident
contexts.description: Tracks and surfaces operational incidents — anomalies, failures, and SLA breaches — with severity classification, escalation paths, and resolution workflows. Athena proactively creates incidents from execution failures and quality signals; operators can acknowledge, escalate, or resolve them. Incidents link back to the triggering executions for drill-down.
contexts.name: incident-management

contexts.api_surface: MCP protocol over stdio/HTTP; Tauri commands: get_mcp_tools, register_mcp_gateway, invoke_mcp_tool
contexts.description: Implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP) — the standard interface for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to LLMs. The desktop app both hosts an MCP server (daemon mode) and consumes external MCP servers via the browser bridge and gateway system. This context owns the core protocol plumbing; tool registration and invocation flow through here.
contexts.name: mcp-integration

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_memories, create_memory, delete_memory, search_memories, compile_memories
contexts.description: Persistent memory and knowledge-base layer that lets personas store and recall structured facts across executions. Memory items are written during execution (or from human review resolutions) and retrieved via semantic lookup. The knowledge base supports both per-persona memories and team-shared memories, with AES-256-GCM encryption for sensitive items.
contexts.name: memories-knowledge

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_model_config, update_model_config, list_available_models, test_byom_endpoint
contexts.description: Allows users to select and tune the LLM model powering each persona, including temperature, context window, thinking budget, and Bring-Your-Own-Model (BYOM) local model support. Exposes an A/B comparison view for evaluating response quality across model variants. BYOM connects to local Ollama or fastembed endpoints and requires the `ml` Cargo feature.
contexts.name: model-configuration

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: start_oauth_flow, refresh_oauth_token, rotate_credential, capture_cli_credential, discover_credentials
contexts.description: Handles OAuth 2.0 authorization flows, token refresh cycles, and credential rotation policies. The OAuth gateway bridges the desktop app to external providers; the rotation engine monitors token expiry and auto-refreshes before executions fail. Includes CLI credential capture for tools that authenticate via terminal, and auto-discovery that scans the system for existing credentials.
contexts.name: oauth-credential-flows

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: sync_obsidian_vault, get_drive_files, extract_ocr, get_obsidian_notes
contexts.description: Integrations for Obsidian Brain (bi-directional vault sync for long-term memory), Google Drive file access, and OCR document extraction. These plugins give personas access to the user's external knowledge and file stores, expanding context beyond what is held in the local SQLite database.
contexts.name: obsidian-drive-plugins

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_onboarding_progress, update_onboarding_step, complete_tour
contexts.description: The guided product tour shown on first launch — step-by-step narrated walkthrough covering core features (design, run, monitor), a persona creation coach, and a tour narration layer that can optionally use live TTS for Athena-narrated guidance. Tour progress is persisted in SQLite and can be re-triggered from Settings.
contexts.name: onboarding-tour

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_overview_metrics, get_saved_views, save_view, get_alert_summary, get_messages_feed
contexts.description: The main observability hub — a customizable widget-based dashboard showing fleet health, execution throughput, cost burn, active personas, and key signal alerts. Each widget is independently data-fetched; the dashboard state (saved views, widget layout) persists per user via SQLite. Acts as the primary landing surface for operators monitoring the agent fleet.
contexts.name: overview-dashboard

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: connect_peer, send_remote_command, sync_cloud, get_network_identity, expose_persona
contexts.description: Optional peer-to-peer mesh network (gated behind the `p2p` Cargo feature) using QUIC transport for encrypted persona-to-persona and device-to-device communication, plus a Node.js cloud-worker reference implementation that runs the same HTTP contract against Alibaba Qwen (DashScope) instead of Claude — enabling cloud-side persona execution without a full Tauri runtime. Provides identity management, enclave-based secure channels, and exposure control for remote persona access.
contexts.name: p2p-network

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_analytics_data, get_heat_map_data, get_throughput_trends, get_cost_breakdown
contexts.description: Provides deeper analysis surfaces beyond the dashboard — execution heat maps, activity timelines, per-persona throughput trends, and token/cost breakdowns. The analytics module aggregates historical execution data and renders it as interactive charts. Used for identifying performance bottlenecks and planning capacity.
contexts.name: performance-analytics

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: start_build_session, stream_design_analysis, compile_genome, evolve_persona, get_genome
contexts.description: AI-assisted wizard that helps users build and evolve persona configurations — prompts, model settings, connectors, and genome parameters. It runs a multi-phase conversation (analyzing → refining → applied) backed by an LLM stream, compiling results into a persona genome stored in SQLite. Key dependencies are the build-session engine, credential vault for connector authentication, and the inference pipeline.
contexts.name: persona-design-wizard

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: update_persona, get_persona, save_persona_draft
contexts.description: The main multi-tab editor surface where users fine-tune a persona after design — system prompt, model config, connectors, tools, and settings. It manages an auto-saving draft cycle via debounced Tauri calls and exposes a diff-aware save indicator. The editor reads from the persona slice and writes back through the personas API.
contexts.name: persona-editor

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: run_persona_test, create_test_suite, get_lab_results, evaluate_output_assertions
contexts.description: Testing and evaluation sandbox where users run head-to-head arena comparisons, define test suites, and review assertion results for a persona. It drives batch test execution against LLM endpoints and aggregates pass/fail metrics, feeding results back into the persona health view. Depends on the execution runner for actually invoking personas and the lab Zustand slice for result state.
contexts.name: persona-lab

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_personas, create_persona, update_persona, delete_persona, duplicate_persona, get_persona_icon
contexts.description: Provides the core CRUD lifecycle for AI personas — creation, listing, filtering, duplication, and deletion. The all-personas view has been fully rebuilt as a DataGrid-based overview surface (`PersonaOverviewPage`) with co-located column definitions, cell renderers, filter hooks, batch-selection bar, card-list layout, health indicators, completeness rings, and a verdict-trend sparkline. Persona data flows through the Zustand agentStore and persists to SQLite via Tauri commands. Depends on vault credentials and template presets for initial persona configuration.
contexts.name: persona-management

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_recipes, adopt_recipe, run_recipe, import_n8n_workflow
contexts.description: A shareable persona use-case library — users browse the recipe gallery, adopt a recipe into a persona, and run it with pre-configured inputs. Recipes abstract common task patterns (summarize, research, monitor) into reusable templates; adoption wires the recipe to the persona's connector and credential config. The n8n transform pipeline imports compatible workflow definitions.
contexts.name: recipe-system

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: run_research, get_research_results, simulate_twin_response, get_twin_config
contexts.description: Two specialized plugins: the Research Lab runs autonomous deep-research workflows (web search, synthesis, citation), and the AI Twin mirrors a persona's behavior model to simulate responses without spending execution quota. Both extend the core agent platform with specialized use-case workflows.
contexts.name: research-lab-twin

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_schedules, create_schedule, update_schedule, delete_schedule, get_next_run
contexts.description: Manages time-based execution scheduling — cron-style rules attached to personas or use cases, countdown timers, and the scheduled-agent overview grid. The Rust scheduler polls the database for due jobs and fires them into the execution engine. The `sub_cron_agents` UI shows which agents are scheduled and their next-run times.
contexts.name: scheduler

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_settings, update_settings, export_data, import_data, get_tier_usage, sync_gitlab
contexts.description: Global application settings — appearance, language, API key management, BYOM endpoints, cloud sync config, tier usage, management API auth, GitLab integration, and data portability (export/import). Settings are persisted via Tauri to a dedicated SQLite table; some settings (e.g., cloud sync) fan out to backend config re-loads.
contexts.name: settings-system

contexts.api_surface: Internal React component library
contexts.description: 173+ reusable UI primitives shared across all feature modules — buttons, modals, form controls, feedback elements, layout shells, display formatters, data grids, and accessibility components. Includes `DataGrid`, a generic paginated table with per-column filtering, sort toggling, animated row reveals via framer-motion, and density-token support. Each component is catalogued with a `@catalog` JSDoc tag; `npm run gen:catalog` regenerates the CATALOG.md index. Using these instead of hand-rolling equivalents is a project-enforced rule.
contexts.name: shared-components

contexts.api_surface: Internal store subscriptions; Tauri event bridge
contexts.description: The Zustand store architecture — root stores, the slice pattern that composes feature-specific sub-stores, and shared selectors. This context is the coordination layer that all feature slices register into; it also owns the event bus singleton and IPC metrics tracking. The `globalThis` pattern ensures store singletons survive Vite HMR without re-initialization.
contexts.name: state-management-core

contexts.api_surface: All Tauri IPC commands; ts-rs generated TypeScript types
contexts.description: The IPC abstraction layer between React and Rust — `invokeWithTimeout` wrappers, generated command name constants, and ts-rs type bindings. All frontend-to-backend calls must go through this layer; an ESLint rule enforces `invokeWithTimeout` and bans raw `invoke`. The `commandNames.generated.ts` file is regenerated on every dev/build cycle.
contexts.name: tauri-bridge

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: send_team_message, get_team_channel, subscribe_channel, add_reaction
contexts.description: Real-time team communication channels where personas and humans exchange messages, directives, and step-boundary receipts during collaborative executions. The channel feed shows a live message stream with read receipts and reaction support; the Rust backend manages channel routing and message delivery guarantees.
contexts.name: team-channels

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_teams, create_team, update_team, delete_team, get_fleet_status, add_team_member
contexts.description: Manages the definition and membership of agent teams — groups of personas that collaborate on shared goals. Teams have a development project link, member roster, and orchestration configuration. The teams UI surfaces the Flight Deck board, team health, and member statuses; the fleet monitor shows all teams with their liveness state.
contexts.name: team-management

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_templates, adopt_template, get_team_presets, adopt_team_preset, submit_template_feedback
contexts.description: A curated library of pre-built persona templates (Starter / Team / Builder tier) that users adopt to instantly create a configured persona. The gallery renders filterable cards; adoption runs a multi-step wizard that wires credentials, customizes parameters, and optionally adds the persona to a team. Team presets bundle multiple persona templates into a one-click team setup.
contexts.name: templates-gallery

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: invoke_tool, list_tools, get_tool_result
contexts.description: Provides the in-app UI and Rust engine support for invoking MCP tools directly during or outside of executions — browsing available tools, sending test invocations, and inspecting results. Acts as a debugging surface for tool integration and feeds tool results back into the execution event stream.
contexts.name: tool-runner

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_use_cases, create_use_case, update_use_case, delete_use_case, schedule_use_case
contexts.description: Manages discrete use cases (task templates) attached to a persona — defining inputs, expected outputs, scheduling config, and linked recipes. The detail view lets users configure and schedule individual use cases while the list surface shows their statuses. Backed by the use_cases Rust command module and the persona_use_cases table.
contexts.name: use-case-management

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: create_workflow, run_workflow, get_workflow_status, get_assignments
contexts.description: The pipeline orchestration layer that coordinates multi-step, multi-persona workflows — sequential and parallel execution chains, conditional branching, and cross-persona handoffs. The Rust composition engine manages workflow state machines; the frontend pipeline store tracks in-progress workflow runs and their per-step status.
contexts.name: workflow-engine

contexts.api_surface: Tauri commands: get_triggers, create_trigger, update_trigger, delete_trigger, test_trigger
contexts.description: Configures the event-driven trigger rules that start persona executions automatically — webhook events, cron schedules, connector signals, and manual dispatch. The trigger editor lets users define conditions, filters, and target personas; the Rust trigger engine evaluates incoming events against stored rules and fires the corresponding executions.
contexts.name: workflow-triggers

use_cases.description: Design, configure and manage a persona end to end — wizard, editor, capabilities and its connectors.
use_cases.name: Agent Authoring

use_cases.description: The KPI-steered dev loop — use cases, KPIs, the director and healing driving work without a human in the loop.
use_cases.name: Autonomous Development

use_cases.description: Store, design and authorise credentials, and bind them to connectors and MCP tools.
use_cases.name: Credential Vault

use_cases.description: See what agents did — runs, history, traces, events, performance and incidents.
use_cases.name: Execution Observability
